title: Beyond Copilot: Building Enterprise AI Agents That Actually Work with Copilot Studio with Manpreet Singh [MVP-MCT]
description:
Building an impressive agent demo is easy, but making agents work reliably in a global enterprise with sensitive data, governance and real users is something else. Microsoft MVP Manpreet Singh explains for architects, IT leaders and makers how to design Copilot Studio agents with clean knowledge, human in the loop, governance, observability and the adoption work that finally delivers ROI.
In this episode
00:00 – Introduction: from Copilot to agents04:48 – Designing an enterprise AI agent11:38 – Knowledge, grounding and data quality14:20 – Actions, integrations and a first agent20:02 – Human in the loop and governance27:50 – Agent lifecycle, Agent 365 and the AI command center45:23 – Observability, testing and multi-agent systems56:22 – Rapid fire and adoption as the key to ROI
Key takeaways
An enterprise agent needs three pillars: a trigger, tools and actions, and clean, well-tagged knowledge sources rather than decades of unfiltered SharePoint content.Governance, DLP and a Center of Excellence should be in place before agents roll out, with policies scoped to what each agent actually needs and tools like Agent 365 providing inventory and observability.The return on AI agents depends mostly on adoption, so every user needs role-based training on what an agent does and what input it expects.
Worth quoting
“So with the AI's, we are not replacing people, we are just empowering them to do their job much better.” – Manpreet Singh (22:28)
“And that also means the difficult part for enterprise technology doesn't disappear. Identity matters, security matters, data quality matters, governance matters, architecture matters, testing matters.” – Mirko Peters (62:45)
